title: The euro stablecoin landscape after MiCA: a selection guide for fintech operators
linkedinPost:
Only 8 euro stablecoins are now legally tradeable in the EU. The rest are gone.

The MiCA grandfathering period closed June 30, 2026. EURT was discontinued. EURS lost its ESMA registration. EURA is winding down. What remains is 8 tokens with a combined market cap of $673.9M — up 128% in 12 months — and a regulatory framework that finally makes euro stablecoin integration a real infrastructure decision for fintech operators.

Here is what I would actually do if I were a fintech COO evaluating this today:

→ Start with EURC for API-first integrations. Circle's custody partnerships (Fireblocks, Anchorage) and exchange liquidity are the most mature.

→ Use EURCV (SG Forge, Société Générale subsidiary) for institutional or bank-to-bank settlement. The issuer credit signal is materially stronger for regulated counterparties.

→ Build ESMA register monitoring into your compliance stack before going live. I run this as a 20-node n8n pipeline — token status changes trigger alerts automatically.

→ Do not integrate any euro stablecoin not on the ESMA register. After June 30, this is a legal exposure question, not a risk management judgment call.

The commercial case: MiCA-compliant euro stablecoins enable 24/7 programmable settlement across 27 EU markets without SEPA batch windows. Revenue per employee improves when settlement infrastructure stops being the bottleneck.

Full piece + the MiCA Compliance Selection Matrix I use for token evaluation — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: Which euro stablecoin has the largest market cap after MiCA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Circle's EURC is the market leader with a market cap of $430.4M as of June 2026, representing approximately 64% of the total MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin market. It rose 109.8% in the 12 months to June 2026 (Decta, June 2026).

mainEntity.name: Is there a full list of MiCA-compliant euro stablecoins?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — the ESMA e-money token register is the authoritative source. As of June 2026, 8 euro-denominated tokens are on the register: EURC, EURCV, EURI, EUROe, EURR, EURD, EUROP, and EURAU. The register is public and updated continuously; any token not on this list does not have legal EMT status in the EU.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a euro stablecoin I am using loses its ESMA registration?

acceptedAnswer.text: You must stop processing or holding the token in any EU-facing product immediately. MiCA's enforcement regime applies to service providers as well as issuers. Continuing to process a de-registered token is a direct breach of EU law, regardless of when the integration was built.

mainEntity.name: How does MiCA's euro stablecoin framework interact with PSD3?

acceptedAnswer.text: MiCA and PSD3 operate in parallel with distinct scopes. MiCA governs the issuance and custody of the token itself. PSD3 governs the payment services built on top of it. A fintech offering euro stablecoin payment services needs both MiCA-compliant token due diligence and a PSD3-compliant payment service framework. They do not substitute for each other.
